answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the lagoon schedule in the opal ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the dune checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Running 172 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
